title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is stratifying the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. Here ν is a number of marked points, apparently treated as unordered: the 'poids marqué' of a vertex counts its marked points, and on the next page the graph 3—2 has Γ = S_3×S_2. The strata are indexed by stable dual graphs, which he calls 'MD-graphes'. For a graph G, the normalized stratum is M̂_G = (∏_α M_{g_α, ν̂_α}) / Γ_G. Here ν̂_α is the number of marked points plus half-edges at α, and Γ_G = Aut(G). 'Dimension modulaire' is dim M̂_G = Σ_α (3g_α − 3 + ν̂_α); 'dimension (modulaire) ambiante' is 3g − 3 + ν; 'codimension modulaire' is the number of edges.

Elementary graphs (previous page). These are the graphs of modular dimension 1. Every vertex is (0,3) except one vertex α0, which is of type (0,4) or (1,1). For them M̂_G ≅ M̂_{0,4} or M̂_{1,1} (eq. 71); their closures are what are now called F-curves.

This page, part 1: the Γ_G-action.
- On M_{1,1} the action is trivial.
- On M_{0,4} it factors through the permutation action on the 4 flags at α0 (eq. 72: Γ_G → S_{Î_{α0}} ≅ S_4).
- He conjectures ('sauf erreur') that the image can be any subgroup of S_4.

Part 2: small ambient dimension.
- Ambient dimension 1 (3g−3+ν = 1) means codimension 0: the one-vertex graphs (0,4) and (1,1) of (70).
- Ambient dimension 2 (M_{0,5} or M_{1,2}) with codimension 1 means one edge, either a loop or a bridge. This gives three graphs:
  (i) vertex with 3 marked points — vertex with 2 marked points, in M_{0,5}. Picture: two lines meeting, points a,b on one and c,d,e on the other.
  (ii) genus-0 vertex with 2 marked points and a loop, in M_{1,2}. This is the irreducible nodal rational curve, Δ_irr.
  (iii) genus-1 vertex — genus-0 vertex with 2 marked points, in M_{1,2}. This is an elliptic tail, Δ_1.
- These are exactly the boundary divisors of M̄_{0,5}/S_5 and M̄_{1,2}/S_2.

On the next page he computes Aut and the image in S_4: S_3×S_2 with image S_3; S_2×S_2 with image S_2×S_2; and S_2. Then he moves on to modular dimension 2. The purpose is the systematic description of the low-dimensional boundary strata (the 'first two levels' of the Teichmüller tower) together with their automorphism data.
errors: Minor imprecision: the action on M_{0,4} factors through S_4, but the Klein four-group V4 ⊂ S_4 acts trivially on M_{0,4}. Double transpositions of 4 points on P^1 are induced by Möbius transformations. So the effective action is through S_4/V4 ≅ S_3, which the page does not note.

The conjecture that every subgroup of S_4 occurs as the image is stated only tentatively ('sauf erreur') and is not proved. For cyclic subgroups like C3 or C4, or for A4 without transpositions, one needs asymmetric 'Frucht-type' trivalent gadgets. It is plausible but unverified here.
Equation number (72) is used twice: once for the map Γ → S_4 and once for the list of three graphs. The next page continues with (73).

ideas.what: Identification of 1-dimensional boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}: all components (0,3) except one, of type (0,4) or (1,1); stratum ≅ M_{0,4} or M_{1,1} modulo Aut(G)
ideas.modern_name: F-curves / 1-dimensional boundary strata (one-dimensional strata of the stable-graph stratification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Faber; Keel–McKernan; Gibney–Keel–Morrison (2002, classification of F-curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses low-dimensional strata and the 'two first levels' principle, but not this explicit list

ideas.what: Action of Aut(G) on the 1-dimensional stratum through the permutation of the 4 flags at the (0,4)-vertex; conjecture that any subgroup of S_4 occurs
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism groups of stable graphs and their action on boundary strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in the combinatorics of M̄_{g,n} boundary strata

ideas.what: Boundary divisors of M̄_{0,5} (unordered) and M̄_{1,2}: one type versus two types (Δ_irr, Δ_1)
ideas.modern_name: Boundary divisors of M̄_{0,5}/S_5 and M̄_{1,2}/S_2

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that the image of Aut(G) in S_4 for elementary (F-curve) graphs can be any subgroup of S_4. This is a small, concrete combinatorial question that is answerable with Frucht-type trivalent graph constructions. It is not explicitly treated in the F-curve literature, though it is a minor point.
missed.quote: L'image de Γ_G dans S_4 doit pouvoir être n'importe quel sous-groupe de S_4, sauf erreur.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of minor interest. It bears on the structure of F-curves in M̄_{g,n}/S_n and on the orbifold structure of the 1-skeleton. The effective action on M_{0,4} is only through S_3 anyway.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard enumeration of 1-dimensional boundary strata (essentially F-curves) and of the boundary divisors in ambient dimension 2. It anticipates the systematic F-curve bookkeeping of later work, but contains nothing a specialist would find new. The only open thread is a small, tentative group-theoretic conjecture.
transcription_corrections: Margin (vertical) reads approximately 'MD-graphes de dim mod 1, dim. modulaire ambiante 2', not 'NB - graphes des dim mod 1, 2...'.
The '28' written above 'de' in the first line appears to be a superscript or reference marker, not part of the formula.

'Ceci donne les trois cas' is closer to 'Ces trois sont les trois cas de dim modulaire ambiante 2, dim modulaire 1'; the crossed-out line 'Dans le cas g_{α0}=0 dans les sommets ... 1' is struck through.
In the third graph the crossed-out label above the left vertex is '4' (struck), and that vertex carries g_{α0}=1, while the right vertex has weight 2 and g_α=0.
The same number (72) is written for both the map Γ_G → S_4 and the list of three graphs.
